task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: shot distance and play-by-play derived roles
methodological_questions: Can role transferability between contexts be tested with n=24 units?
How should cut-heavy versus drive-heavy shaper classification be validated and kept stable across seasons and playoffs?
What sample size, exposure, and reliability constraints apply when comparing role transfer across players or teams?
What risks arise from outcome-derived labels, lookahead leakage, and regression to the mean in role classification?

historical_evidence.finding: In 92 connector movers, pre-move cut share (vs drive share) was associated with whether connector function reproduced after a move (rho +0.265, p=0.011; LOO AUC 0.622; permutation p=0.005; holds when dropping Gafford). Recorded as exploratory; most other pre-move predictors were null, and the paper treats cut share as a boundary condition, applying to connectors only.

Tested whether matching a mover's initiation diet to a destination's thin jobs predicts post-move outcomes. Of 198 movers, 19 were taxonomy connectors and the 15.7% match rate left 5 matched connectors. The all-movers binary result (p=0.0283) did not hold as a continuous Spearman (-0.034). Verdict recorded as null.

DRIVE-as-BEST counter tested against a feasibility-constrained play-type mix on 44 triggers from 13 teams. Observed gap (-0.066 PPP, p=0.2175) was below the minimum detectable effect (0.180 PPP at 80% power, SD about 0.34), so a null and an effect up to 0.18 PPP could not be distinguished.

Archived check of whether mover portability relates to destination net-rating change. Recorded as underpowered and null once corrected for landing-spot quality; no numbers kept; dropped from Paper 1. Verdict recorded as null.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Connector-specific mover tests on a binary diet-match split within a small mover sample
failed_approaches.why: Only 19 taxonomy connectors and 5 matched connectors; the all-movers binary p-value did not replicate as a continuous Spearman (-0.034), so the result was not a licensed connector test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Counter-effect test of DRIVE-as-BEST against a constrained play-type mix on 44 triggers
failed_approaches.why: Observed gap was below the minimum detectable effect (0.180 PPP), so the test could not distinguish a true null from a practically meaningful effect; recorded limit is small sample and low power.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Destination on-court net-rating checks for movers
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as underpowered and null only after a landing-spot correction; no numbers were kept, so the result cannot be reused as evidence.

evidence_establishes: In one earlier study family ([prior work][prior work], n=92 connector movers), pre-move cut share was positively associated with connector function reproducing after a move, recorded as exploratory with a permutation p=0.005.

Earlier mover and counter-effect tests in this project on samples of 19 to 198 units were recorded as underpowered, untestable, or null, showing that subgroup and binary-split designs on this kind of data have repeatedly failed to deliver a decisive test.
The earlier evidence shows that the cut-share signal was recorded for connectors specifically, not for shapers in general.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests cut-heavy versus drive-heavy shapers as a question; the supported result concerns connectors ([prior work][prior work]), so it does not directly establish the shaper claim.
The retrieved records do not establish that the cut-share result replicates out of sample, across seasons, or in playoffs.

Nothing in the retrieved evidence shows that a test with 24 units has adequate power; the closest comparable power analyses used n=44 and n=92 and were recorded as underpowered or supported with a small-sample limit.
Whether the 'unit' of n=24 refers to teams, players, or movers is not stated in the task, and no record covers that unit.
own_inferences: With n=24, a two-sided Spearman test at alpha 0.05 and 80% power can detect only a fairly large correlation (roughly |rho| of 0.55 or more), far above the +0.265 effect recorded in SF-[prior work], so a null at n=24 would be uninformative.
The n=92 result in SF-[prior work] is unlikely to transfer to n=24 units; its permutation and AUC figures depend on a sample nearly four times larger.
Because cut share and portability are both derived from the same play-by-play-based possession records, any pre-move label that is built from outcomes of the same season risks leakage.
The question as posed ('travel better') needs an operational definition of portability that is not outcome-derived; none of the retrieved records supplies one for shapers.
uncertainties: The definition of the 24 units, the portability outcome, and the cut/drive classification threshold are not given in the task.
Stability of cut-share classification across 2022-23 to 2025-26 and between regular season and playoffs is unknown.
The 2025-26 playoffs file is partial before 2026-06-21 and the regular season is partial before 2026-04-13, so any analysis run before those dates would use incomplete data.
The status 'supported' in SF-[prior work] is [prior work]'s own verdict; this review has not verified its numbers against source data.
Record SF-[prior work] gives no numbers, so its null verdict cannot be checked.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the retrieved records, the planned design might have been a shaper-level test on the full set of units. The retrieved records show that (a) the only positive cut-share result came from a larger connector-only sample (n=92) that is not comparable to n=24, and (b) three earlier tests on smaller samples were recorded as untestable or underpowered. This moved the decision from a pre-registration of a shaper test to do_not_proceed as posed, with a descriptive or reframed alternative offered instead.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 units gives low power to detect the modest effect size seen in the only supporting record (rho +0.265 at n=92); a null would be uninformative.
Cut and drive shares are estimated from play-by-play counts per player-season; low-usage units will have unstable shares, and some shaper-season cells may be empty.
Play-type and shot-distance classifications may be noisy; no reliability check of the cut/drive labels is recorded.
Portability is defined by post-move function or outcome, so it risks being derived from the same possession records used to build the predictor.

prior_work.summary: [prior work][prior work] reports a supported, exploratory positive association between pre-move cut share and connector portability in 92 movers. It covers connectors, not shapers, and is recorded as a boundary condition rather than a general result. [prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work] are recorded as untestable or underpowered and do not answer the shaper question. The question is therefore partly addressed for a neighbouring population, not answered for cut-heavy versus drive-heavy shapers with 24 units.

risks.text: With 24 units the test is badly underpowered for effects of the size recorded in earlier work (rho +0.265 at n=92; MDE 0.180 PPP at n=44 in a related counter test).
Shares of cut and drive plays depend on exposure; low-minute shapers or thin shot-distance coverage will give unreliable classifications.
No reliability check of the cut/drive labels across seasons or between regular season and playoffs is recorded.
Units selected for extreme cut or drive shares, or for a strong season, will tend to regress toward the mean in later seasons, inflating apparent transfer.
If the portability label is built from the same play-by-play outcomes that define shaper roles, the association can be circular.
Using full-season or playoff play-by-play to classify roles before a move, then testing transfer on the same data, lets future information enter the predictor.
Team context, usage, lineup quality, and landing-spot quality can drive both cut share and post-move outcome; SF-[prior work] recorded that landing-spot correction was needed.
Testing cut and drive shares, several outcome definitions, and position splits increases false positives; SF-[prior work] itself ran many predictors and treated most as null.
Without a placebo such as drive share or a shuffled label, a positive cut-share result cannot be separated from structure in the classification.
Shot-distance and play-type tagging and league-wide style change across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may shift the cut/drive mix over time.

design.estimand: Not recommended as posed. Minimum viable alternative: the association between a pre-move cut-share (cut minus drive share) and a pre-specified, outcome-independent portability measure, descriptive only, with no causal or transfer claim.
design.unit: Must be fixed before analysis; the task does not say whether the 24 units are teams, players, or movers. Suggested unit: player-season, one row per mover.
design.sample: 24 units as recorded; the only comparable prior sample was n=92 (SF-[prior work]), which does not transfer. Use only complete files: regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 and 2025-26 regular season after 2026-04-13; exclude the 2025-26 playoffs until complete after 2026-06-21.
design.power: At n=24 and alpha 0.05 two-sided, power of 80% requires |rho| of about 0.55 or more (my inference, not a recorded figure); the recorded +0.265 effect is far below that. The test would be underpowered, so no pre-registered confirmatory claim is licensed.
design.controls: Pre-specify minutes or possessions threshold, team pace and usage, landing-spot quality, season fixed effects, and a drive-share placebo. Compute cut/drive shares from a pre-move window only, with no post-move data (no lookahead).
design.falsification: Drive share as a negative-control predictor; shuffled outcome labels (5000 permutations as in SF-[prior work]); split-half or season-to-season stability of the cut/drive classification before any outcome test.
design.multiplicity: Single pre-specified primary predictor (cut share) and single primary outcome; all other predictors and outcomes labelled exploratory with correction (e.g., Holm or BH).
design.decision_rule: Proceed with a descriptive reliability and exposure report only. Any claim that cut-heavy roles transfer better requires a larger pre-registered sample (gather more units) or external data; otherwise report 'untestable at n=24'.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season only after 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs only after 2026-06-21. Snapshot the file date with the analysis.
